trickyParts: The hub signals every wake after each LISTEN, so each woken loop runs one extra pass shortly after boot; a process that found a lease held retries every HeldRetry until a pass of its own runs (multiprocess test rewritten to that rule).

write_suggestions.id is a uuid and suggestions commit outside the events' commit-order lock, so the sweep tracks new suggestions with a swept column (0125, added default true then default false: no rewrite) and the event log with a cursor (0124); a 60 s settle window keeps a comment and the agent's follow-up update judged together.

Suggestion cursor relies on events.id committing in id order (events.Broker.Append's commit-order lock); dispatch://INFRA-591 replaces that with events.Horizon and has this sweep on its consumer list.
deviations: Plan items 2h (architecture importer shared sync) and 2i (redelivery pending index) are not in this PR: they build on INFRA-562, which has not merged; the architect split them to dispatch://INFRA-627.

Idle measurements ran before and after side by side (own database, NATS, listener and ports each, slots swapped between runs) instead of alternating one at a time; the 1x step ran one process at a time as planned.

pg_stat_statements is not in the pgserver build, so statements were counted from log_statement=all (the plan's fallback); config B's template was embedded by the head binary, so the before build's B runs ran on schema 0126 (migrations written to keep the previous release working).
Suggestion outcome cursor holds event_id only (no suggestion_id): suggestions use the swept column instead, for the reason under trickyParts.
discoveredComplexity: Two api tests fail only on this pod's test Postgres: TestIssueRanksStayOrderedPastLowercaseDigitsAndProductionShapedMoves needs a database whose collation is not byte order (this initdb has only C locales), and TestSavingAPathologicalBodyIsBounded is a timing bound that failed under full-suite CPU contention and passes alone.
